name: Cloud_Types_Educational

questions.question: How does cloud-type identification skill function as weather-prediction human capital, where accurate forecasting enables optimal timing of farming, solar charging, mining, and travel decisions?
questions.answer: Cloud literacy is a force-multiplier in the survival economy. A player who identifies cumulonimbus delays mining to avoid flash-flood risk; one who reads cirrus maximizes solar charging before cloud cover increases. The differential is measurable: weather-blind players lose 15-25% of expedition value to weather disruption, while cloud-literate players achieve near-100% scheduling efficiency.

questions.question: Do the different cloud types (cirrus, cumulus, stratus, nimbostratus) tell the story of what the weather will do next, teaching the player to read the sky like a pilot or farmer?
questions.answer: Cloud types are a readable weather forecast: cirrus warns of approaching fronts, cumulus tells of thermal uplift, stratus promises drizzle, nimbostratus threatens persistent rain — the sky narrates tomorrow.

questions.question: Can the player distinguish cloud types (cumulus, stratus, cirrus, nimbostratus, cumulonimbus) by shape, altitude, and color without needing to open a reference UI or pause gameplay?
questions.answer: Each cloud type uses distinct shape profiles (puffy sheets for cumulus, flat layers for stratus, wispy streaks for cirrus). Altitude banding helps identification. Educational labels appear on first hover.

questions.question: Does the player's cloud-type identification progress (which clouds they have scanned, learned about, identified correctly) need to persist?
questions.answer: Yes. The player's cloud identification journal records which cloud types they have scanned. This is player progression state and must save. Written when the player scans a new cloud type (infrequent, once per type).

questions.question: Does the cloud classification system teach real cloud physics (cumulus convection, stratus stratification, cirrus ice crystal formation) or just visual identification?
questions.answer: Both. Visual identification (shape, color, altitude) is the primary interaction, but each scan also explains the meteorological physics: warm air rising for cumulus, stable layers for stratus, high-altitude ice for cirrus.
